heroText: Torshavn is one of the world's smallest capitals, a harbour town of turf roofs, ferries and weather-shaped island life. Start at Tinganes, visit Torshavn Cathedral and the Nordic House, then use the harbour lanes as a base for trips to Kirkjubour or northern viewpoints. Vagar Airport is the Faroe Islands' flight gateway.

areas.name: Torshavn harbour
areas.text: The harbour area is best for first stays, restaurants, ferry atmosphere and walks into Tinganes.

areas.name: Tinganes
areas.text: Tinganes is atmospheric and historic, with turf-roofed government buildings and lanes close to central hotels.

areas.name: Hoyvik
areas.text: Hoyvik is a quieter residential base north of the centre, useful for apartments and car-based island trips.

areas.name: Argir
areas.text: Argir sits across the water from central Torshavn, offering calmer stays and quick road access south.

airports.name: Vagar Airport (FAE)
airports.text: Vagar Airport is the Faroe Islands' only commercial airport, connected to Torshavn by road tunnel, buses and transfers.

airportTransfer.value: 40-50 min by car or airport bus from Vagar Airport

stayOverview: Stay by Torshavn harbour for restaurants and ferry atmosphere, Tinganes for old-town character, Hoyvik for apartments and drivers, or Argir for quieter views and easier southern road access.
hotelIntro: Torshavn is compact, but weather and island routes make logistics important. Harbour stays are easiest without a car, while Hoyvik and Argir suit travellers driving to villages, tunnels and ferry connections.
rentalCars: A rental car is very useful in the Faroe Islands, though central Torshavn itself is walkable.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Stay near the harbour if you want restaurants, ferries and central walks without needing the car every evening.

history.text: According to romantics, the main ting for the islands was convoked in Tórshavn in 825, on Tinganes, the peninsula that divides the harbour into two parts: Eystaravág and Vestaravág.

history.label: 9th century
history.text: The Viking settlers in the 9th century established their own parliaments, called tings, in different parts of the islands, it being the tradition in each case to hold the ting at a neutral and thus uninhabited place, so no one location gave anyone an advantage.

history.label: 12th century
history.text: During the 12th century, all trade between Norway and the Faroes, along with other tributary islands to the west, became centralised in Bergen.
In 1271, a royal trade monopoly was established in Tórshavn by the Norwegian Crown.
In c. 1580 a small fort, Skansin, was built by the Faroese naval hero and trader Magnus Heinason at the north end of the harbour.
Conditions improved in Tórshavn when the trade monopoly became a royal monopoly in 1709.
Tórshavn Cathedral was first built in 1788 and partly rebuilt in 1865.
